title: I Built an App the Government Doesn't Want You to See
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: Promotes GovDealFinder and Replit Agent 4; the transcript does not state whether there is a paid relationship or provide independently verified operating results.

stated_problem.quote: Filtering is a nightmare. Most people give up before they ever find anything.
stated_problem.speaker: Chris Koerner

idea.name: GovDealFinder contract search tool
idea.one_liner: A searchable government-contract tool for small businesses and aspiring owners, with no revenue model stated.
idea.customer: Small businesses and aspiring owners looking for federal government contracts, including set-aside opportunities.
idea.offer: A web app that searches contract listings by business type and state, shows contract dollar amounts, and is intended to offer email alerts for matching new listings.
idea.revenue_model: Not stated; no pricing or monetization model is described.

key_quotes.quote: So, what I wanted to do is to build something that makes this dead simple.
Type in what your business does, pick your state, and see contracts you can actually bid on with dollar amounts.
I would love for it to have a email collection field so people can be notified when new government contracts are posted that meet their filters.
I wanted to build a business in the government contract space because Google Trends and AHRefs and all these other random tools were screaming at me, there's opportunity here.
And if you want to go look at government contracts, check out govdealfiner.com cuz I just built it right in front of you.

claims.claim: The US government spent $834 billion on contracts last year.
claims.quote: The US government spent $834 billion on contracts last year, and most small business owners don't even know this money exists.

claims.claim: SAM.gov receives 2.2 million visits per month.
claims.quote: This website gets 2.2 million visits a month, and it's an ugly website.

claims.claim: A comparable website would normally cost between 10 and 20,000 to build and take weeks or months of back and forth.
claims.quote: Now, a website like this would normally cost between 10 and 20,000 to build, plus a team of developers, and weeks or months of going back and forth.

claims.claim: The app build took about 4 minutes.
claims.quote: Look at that. Okay, that took about 4 minutes.

claims.claim: The speaker repeats that the US government spent 834 billion on contracts last year.
claims.quote: Wow, the US government spent 834 billion on contracts last year.

claims.claim: The speaker asked the app builder to add three to five blog posts to improve search visibility.
claims.quote: Now I'm asking it to add three to five blog posts that will help my site appear better in search results when looking for government contracts.

claims.claim: A generated landing-page variation displayed copy saying 347 contracts were closing that week; the transcript does not verify that figure.
claims.quote: 347 contracts are closing this week. Don't let them slip away.
And look at that, it is. So, I'm going to spend 12 bucks, buy the domain name, and go ahead and link it to this Replit project, and click publish.

claims.claim: The speaker says the government awards almost a trillion dollars in contracts each year, with about 200 billion reserved for small businesses.
claims.quote: And remember, the government hands out almost a trillion dollars a year in contracts and about 200 billion of that is reserved for small businesses.

claims.claim: The speaker describes eligible small businesses as having under 10 employees, including zero employees.
claims.quote: Those are businesses with under 10 employees, even zero employees.

acquisition_channels.details: Asked the app builder to add three to five blog posts intended to improve search visibility for government contracts.
Demonstrates the tool in the video and directs viewers to the live website.

ideas.delivery: A published web app that retrieves contract data using a SAM.gov API key and lets users search listings; email alerts for matching new listings were requested as a feature.

prices: 10 to 20,000 for a typical website build; currency not stated

ideas.other_uk_rules: For UK users, email alerts and any marketing emails would need to comply with PECR and UK GDPR. If a paid recurring subscription is introduced, assess the DMCC Act subscription rules.

idea.name: Tree trimming business
idea.one_liner: A tree trimming service that can use government contract listings to find public-sector work; no pricing or operating details are given.
idea.customer: Not stated; the demo uses a government tree trimming contract listing.
idea.revenue_model: Paid tree trimming jobs; pricing is not stated.

key_quotes.quote: I own a tree trimming business, so this is the preview.
This should work as it actually works in real life.

claims.claim: The app demo showed a tree trimming contract posted March 9th by the Department of Defense.
claims.quote: There it is. Posted March 9th, Department of Defense.

ideas.delivery: Tree trimming work would be delivered physically; the transcript only mentions the business while testing a government-contract search tool.
